grammarChart.passive: Object + has/have + been + Past Participle + (by + Subject)
Object + will + be + Past Participle + (by + Subject)

explanation: The passive voice is used when the action or the object of the action is more important than the person or thing performing the action. It shifts the focus from the doer to the receiver of the action. The basic structure of the passive voice is the appropriate form of the verb 'to be' (am, is, are, was, were, been, will be) followed by the past participle of the main verb.
keyRules: Identify the object of the active sentence. This becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
Use the correct form of the verb 'to be' that matches the tense of the original active verb and the new subject.
Use the past participle of the main verb.
The original subject can be omitted or introduced with 'by' if it is important or unknown.
azarNotes: In Indonesian, the passive voice is often formed by adding 'di-' to the verb. For example, 'Membaca' (to read) becomes 'Dibaca' (is read).

When translating from Indonesian to English passive, pay close attention to the tense. The 'di-' prefix doesn't explicitly indicate tense, so you'll need to infer it from context or add auxiliary verbs.
The 'by + agent' phrase is optional in the passive voice. It's often omitted when the agent is unknown, unimportant, or obvious.

examples.passive: The meal is prepared by the chef.
A new planet was discovered by scientists.

examples.active: The company has hired new employees.
examples.passive: New employees have been hired by the company.

examples.active: The government will implement new policies.
examples.passive: New policies will be implemented by the government.

commonMistakes: Using the wrong form of 'to be'. For example, 'The book is wrote' instead of 'The book was written'.
Forgetting to use the past participle. For example, 'The cake is bake' instead of 'The cake is baked'.
Incorrectly changing the tense when converting to passive.
Overusing the passive voice, making the writing sound impersonal or vague.
ieltsTip: In IELTS Writing Task 2, the passive voice is useful for discussing general truths, processes, or when you want to sound more objective and formal. For example, when describing a process or discussing societal issues, the passive voice can be very effective. However, avoid overusing it, as it can make your writing sound unnatural. Use it strategically to emphasize the action or the recipient of the action.

quiz.question: Choose the correct passive form of the following sentence: 'The students completed the project.'
options: The project completed by the students.
The project was completed by the students.
The project is completed by the students.
The project has completed by the students.
quiz.answer: The project was completed by the students.

quiz.question: Choose the correct passive form of the following sentence: 'The artist is painting a portrait.'
options: A portrait is painted by the artist.
A portrait was painting by the artist.
A portrait is being painted by the artist.
A portrait has been painting by the artist.
quiz.answer: A portrait is being painted by the artist.

quiz.question: Choose the correct passive form of the following sentence: 'The committee will announce the results next week.'
options: The results will announce next week by the committee.
The results will be announce next week by the committee.
The results will be announced next week by the committee.
The results are announced next week by the committee.
quiz.answer: The results will be announced next week by the committee.

quiz.question: Choose the correct passive form of the following sentence: 'They have built a new bridge.'
options: A new bridge has built.
A new bridge is built.
A new bridge has been built.
A new bridge was built.
quiz.answer: A new bridge has been built.

quiz.question: Which sentence is NOT in the passive voice?
options: The book was written by a famous author.
The experiment is conducted carefully.
The students are studying for their exams.
The report has been submitted.
quiz.answer: The students are studying for their exams.
